We also find merit in the Petitioner’s submission that Article 8.6 of the PPA specifically provides a mechanism where the Procurer disputes a Monthly Bill or a Supplementary Bill. In the present case, admittedly, the Respondents acknowledged the Supplementary Bills and did not invoke the dispute resolution mechanism contemplated under Article 8.6 within the stipulated period (and in the absence of raising any dispute by the due date, a provisional/ supplementary bill shall be taken as conclusive). Therefore, while the Respondents were certainly entitled to seek clarifications for the purpose of verification, the same cannot have the effect of postponing the Due Date prescribed under the contract, particularly when the Procurer failed to dispute the Bill in terms of Article 8.6 of the PPA. # **_ Issue (C): Whether the Petitioner's acceptance of payments under the Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge and Related Matters) Rules, 2022 precludes it from claiming the disputed balance LPS? _** monthly instalments. According to them, permitting the Petitioner to raise additional claims for the same period would defeat the very object of the statutory scheme and result in reopening dues that had already been settled between the parties. The real question is whether the Petitioner's participation in the statutory payment mechanism amounts to an unequivocal relinquishment of its right to pursue the disputed balance LPS under the PPA. 40. It is a settled principle that waiver involves the intentional and unequivocal abandonment of a known legal right. Such intention must be clear, conscious and unequivocal. A reservation of rights made contemporaneously with acceptance of payment is fundamentally inconsistent with any inference that the party intended to abandon its remaining claim. In the present case, the Petitioner's acceptance of the payment mechanism was expressly qualified by a reservation that the disputed balance LPS would be pursued separately. In these circumstances, we cannot accept the Respondents' contention that the Petitioner waived its claim. party. Where a dispute subsists regarding the computation of contractual dues, such dispute necessarily remains subject to adjudication in accordance with the governing contract and the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003. 42. In the present case, the dispute pertains to the computation of the contractual LPS payable under the PPA, arising from the Respondents' interpretation of the Due Date for payment of the Change in Law Supplementary Bills. As held while deciding Issue Nos. (A) and (B), the Petitioner's claim for the differential LPS survives independently of the statutory mechanism adopted for liquidation of the admitted dues. The acceptance of payment under the LPS Rules, 2022, accompanied by an express reservation of rights, cannot operate as a bar to adjudication of the disputed balance claim. 47. We have considered the above submissions. The Respondents' objection proceeds on the premise that the Petitioner is not entitled to the differential LPS claimed in the present Petition. However, while deciding Issue Nos. (A) to (C), we have already held that the Respondents were not justified in postponing the Due Date by linking it to the completion of verification of the Supplementary Bills, that the Petitioner is entitled to the differential LPS computed in accordance with the PPA, and that acceptance of payment under the LPS Rules, 2022 does not extinguish the Petitioner's claim. Consequently, the very foundation of the Respondents' objection does not survive.
